title.en: Christianization of Armenia

summary.en: King Tiridates III of Armenia, under the influence of Saint Gregory the Illuminator, establishes Christianity as the state religion, making Armenia the first Christian nation. This event not only consolidates the Armenian people but also paves the way for the legalization of Christianity in the Roman Empire, deeply influencing the history of the Caucasus region.

title.en: Sasanian Empire clashes with the Kushan Empire on the border

summary.en: Under the rule of Persian Emperor Narseh, the Sasanian Dynasty launches a series of border offensives against the declining Kushan Empire to secure the eastern frontiers and control Central Asian trade routes. title.en: Internal conflicts intensify within the Roman Tetrarchy

summary.en: The Tetrarchy system established by Roman Emperor Diocletian falls into turmoil due to succession issues. After the forced abdication of Western Augustus Maximian, relations between his son Maxentius and Eastern Augustus Galerius deteriorate. The breakdown of trust among the emperors sets the stage for a larger civil war, ultimately leading to the collapse of the Tetrarchy.

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝戴克里先创立的四帝共治制因继承人问题陷入动荡。

title.en: Diocletian issues the harshest edict against Christianity

summary.en: Roman Emperor Diocletian, aiming to restore traditional polytheistic religion and strengthen imperial authority, issues the most severe persecution edict in imperial history, ordering the destruction of churches, confiscation of scriptures, prohibition of Christians from holding public office, and mandatory sacrifices. Christian leaders and believers in regions such as the Dioc

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝戴克里先为恢复传统多神教信仰、加强皇权权威，颁布了帝国史上最严厉的基督教迫害敕令。命令各地摧毁教堂、没收经书、禁止基督徒担任公职，并强制献祭。尼西亚总督区等地的基督教领袖和信众遭受了大规模处决与酷刑，史称“大迫害”。
statement.en:
Roman Emperor Diocletian, aiming to restore traditional polytheistic religion and strengthen imperial authority, issues the most severe persecution edict in imperial history, ordering the destruction of churches, confiscation of scriptures, prohibition of Christians from holding public office, and mandatory sacrifices. Christian leaders and believers in regions such as the Diocese of Nicomedia suffer mass executions and torture, known as the 'Great Persecution'.

For Europe in 303 CE, “Diocletian issues the harshest edict against Christianity” is a traceable node of Religion change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 罗马皇帝戴克里先为恢复传统多神教信仰、加强皇权权威，颁布了帝国史上最严厉的基督教迫害敕令。命令各地摧毁教堂、没收经书、禁止基督徒担任公职，并强制献祭。尼西亚总督区等地的基督教领袖和信众遭受了大规模处决与酷刑，史称“大迫害”。

Christian leaders and believers in regions such as the Diocese of Nicomedia suffer mass executions and torture, known as the 'Great Persecution'.

title.en: Roman Emperor Diocletian formally abdicates, beginning the end of the Tetrarchy

summary.en: The Tetrarchy system established by Roman Emperor Diocletian to end the Crisis of the Third Century collapses due to succession problems. title.en: Christianity expands rapidly in the Kingdom of Aksum, growing influence of the Alexandrian diocese

title.en: Maxentius proclaims himself emperor in Rome

summary.en: Maxentius, son of former Emperor Maximian, uses discontent among the Roman Senate and Praetorian Guard over tax policies to incite a rebellion in Rome, proclaiming himself emperor. He controls Italy, Africa, and other regions, forming a three-way standoff with Eastern Emperor Galerius and Western Emperor Constantine, resulting in multiple emperors ruling simultaneously.

title.en: Large-scale excavation of Buddhist grottoes begins in northern China

summary.en: With the deepening spread of Buddhism in northern China, monks and believers begin carving grottoes and sculpting Buddha images on cliffs along major thoroughfares, creating spaces for meditation and worship. statement.zh: 随着佛教在中国北方的深入传播，僧侣与信徒开始在交通要道沿线的山崖上开凿石窟，雕刻佛像，作为禅修和礼拜的场所。甘肃天梯山石窟等早期石窟开始营造，这一艺术形式将印度佛教造像与中国传统雕刻技法结合，开启了长达1000年的中国石窟寺营造传统。
statement.en:
With the deepening spread of Buddhism in northern China, monks and believers begin carving grottoes and sculpting Buddha images on cliffs along major thoroughfares, creating spaces for meditation and worship. Early grottoes, such as the Tiantishan Grottoes in Gansu, are excavated during this period. This art form combines Indian Buddhist iconography with traditional Chinese carving techniques, initiating a thousand-year tradition of Chinese grotto temple construction.

statement.zh: 经过八王之乱，东海王司马越完全掌控朝政。他废黜并毒死了毫无实权的晋惠帝司马衷，拥立其弟豫章王司马炽为帝，是为晋怀帝。改元永嘉。晋怀帝试图恢复皇权，但朝政大权仍掌握在司马越手中，西晋的统治已名存实亡。

After the War of the Eight Princes, the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, fully controls the court. He deposes and poisons the powerless Emperor Hui of Jin, then installs his brother, the Prince of Yuzhang Sima Chi, as Emperor Huai of Jin, changing the era name to Yongjia. Emperor Huai attempts to restore imperial power, but real authority remains with Sima Yue; the Western Jin's rule exists in name only.

title.en: Roman Emperor Galerius issues an Edict of Toleration on his deathbed, halting Christian persecution

summary.en: While gravely ill in Nicomedia, Eastern Emperor Galerius issues an edict admitting that the persecution of Christians has failed to achieve its aims, allowing Christians to hold religious assemblies and pray for him. title.en: Shi Le occupies Xiangguo, establishing a solid base

title.en: Rome completes the Arch of Constantine

summary.en: To honor Constantine's victory over Maxentius, Rome raised a triple-bayed triumphal arch beside the Via Triumphalis, reusing portraits of earlier emperors, a hallmark of imperial monumentality.

statement.zh:
罗马为纪念君士坦丁击败马克森提乌斯，于大道旁建三拱凯旋门。它把新胜绩与旧帝雕像并置：一方面宣告当前皇帝的合法性，另一方面借前代形象把胜利接入罗马纪念传统。三拱形制与大道旁的选址，使它既是仪式通道，也是帝国纪念建筑的代表。

把「罗马建成君士坦丁凯旋门」放回公元312年的罗马，可以看到建筑变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: The Milan agreement: religious toleration and Christian legal status

summary.en: In February 313 Constantine and Licinius met at Milan and concluded a political agreement of religious toleration; the surviving copies are Licinius's June letter to the eastern provinces. The agreement granted all persons freedom of worship, assured Christians the right to organise churches and recover property, and ended systematic persecution, but did not make Christianity t

statement.zh: 313年2月，君士坦丁与李锡尼在米兰会晤，达成一项政治协议；现存副本是李锡尼于313年6月贴在帝国东部的那份通函。
statement.en: In February 313 Constantine and Licinius met at Milan and concluded a political agreement; the surviving copies are the letter Licinius posted in the eastern empire in June 313.

sources.locator: Britannica, Edict of Milan, opening paragraph
sources.excerpt: It was the outcome of a political agreement concluded in Mediolanum (modern Milan) between the Roman emperors Constantine I and Licinius in February 313.

sources.locator: Britannica, Edict of Milan, opening paragraph
sources.excerpt: The extant copies of this decree are actually those posted by Licinius in the eastern parts of the empire in June 313.

zh: 313年2月，君士坦丁与李锡尼在米兰会晤，达成一项政治协议；现存副本是李锡尼于313年6月贴在帝国东部的那份通函。
en: In February 313 Constantine and Licinius met at Milan and concluded a political agreement; the surviving copies are the letter Licinius posted in the eastern empire in June 313.

note.zh: 写“政治协议/通函”，不写“君士坦丁单独颁布”。
note.en: Calls it a political agreement/letter, not a unilateral Constantinian edict.

statement.zh: 协议宣布所有人都有崇拜自己神祇的自由，保证基督徒的合法权利，包括组织教会，并命令归还迫害期间没收的个人与团体财产。
statement.en: The agreement granted all persons freedom to worship their own deities, assured Christians of legal rights including the right to organise churches, and ordered the return of personal and corporate property confiscated during persecution.

sources.locator: Britannica, Edict of Milan, opening paragraph
sources.excerpt: The Edict of Milan was a proclamation that established religious toleration for Christianity within the Roman Empire, concluded between emperors Constantine I and Licinius in 313. The edict granted Christians legal rights, including the right to organize churches, and directed the return of confiscated property, ending systematic imperial persecution.

sources.locator: Britannica, Edict of Milan, opening paragraph
sources.excerpt: The edict did not establish Christianity as the official religion of the Roman Empire, but rather granted all persons freedom to worship whatever deity they pleased.

zh: 协议宣布所有人都有崇拜自己神祇的自由，保证基督徒的合法权利，包括组织教会，并命令归还迫害期间没收的个人与团体财产。
en: The agreement granted all persons freedom to worship their own deities, assured Christians of legal rights including the right to organise churches, and ordered the return of personal and corporate property confiscated during persecution.

note.zh: 崇拜自由、组织教会、归还财产三条照条目。
note.en: Worship freedom, church organisation and property return follow the entry.

statement.zh: 它结束了系统性的帝国迫害，但没有把基督教立为国教；基督教国教地位是381年狄奥多西一世时期的事，传统罗马祭祀也未被禁止。
statement.en: It ended systematic imperial persecution but did not make Christianity the state religion; that came under Theodosius I in 381, and traditional Roman cults were not prohibited.

sources.locator: Britannica, Edict of Milan, 'Influence and legacy'
sources.excerpt: The Edict of Milan did not make Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire (this was instituted later, under Theodosius I in 381), nor did it prohibit traditional Roman religious practices.

zh: 它结束了系统性的帝国迫害，但没有把基督教立为国教；基督教国教地位是381年狄奥多西一世时期的事，传统罗马祭祀也未被禁止。
en: It ended systematic imperial persecution but did not make Christianity the state religion; that came under Theodosius I in 381, and traditional Roman cults were not prohibited.

note.zh: 国教日期写381年；有的文献写380年，正文不展开。
note.en: Establishment is dated 381; some accounts say 380, not discussed in the body.

statement.zh: 君士坦丁此后赞助教会建筑，并于325年召集尼西亚会议；基督教从被迫害的少数派走向受国家庇护的宗教。
statement.en: Constantine afterwards patronised church building and convened the Council of Nicaea in 325; Christianity moved from a persecuted minority to a religion protected by the state.

sources.locator: Britannica, Edict of Milan, 'Influence and legacy'
sources.excerpt: Constantine also began issuing laws conveying upon the church and its clergy fiscal and legal privileges and immunities from civic burdens. He also became increasingly involved in ecclesiastical affairs, most notably by convening the First Council of Nicaea in 325, which sought to resolve theological disputes within the church and produced a creed.

zh: 君士坦丁此后赞助教会建筑，并于325年召集尼西亚会议；基督教从被迫害的少数派走向受国家庇护的宗教。
en: Constantine afterwards patronised church building and convened the Council of Nicaea in 325; Christianity moved from a persecuted minority to a religion protected by the state.

note.zh: 赞助教会与尼西亚会议照条目；不写“基督教立刻成为多数”。
note.en: Patronage and Nicaea follow the entry; no immediate majority claim.

statement.zh: “米兰敕令”是后世称呼，实质是两位皇帝的政治协议与致总督通函；它的意义不是“基督教成为国教”，而是宗教宽容与财产归还。
statement.en: 'Edict of Milan' is a later name; in substance it was a political agreement between two emperors and a letter to governors, and its significance lies in toleration and property restitution, not in making Christianity the state religion.

zh: “米兰敕令”是后世称呼，实质是两位皇帝的政治协议与致总督通函；它的意义不是“基督教成为国教”，而是宗教宽容与财产归还。
en: 'Edict of Milan' is a later name; in substance it was a political agreement between two emperors and a letter to governors, and its significance lies in toleration and property restitution, not in making Christianity the state religion.

note.zh: 作者判断：名称与实质分开，避免“国教化”误读。
note.en: Author judgment: separates name from substance and avoids the 'establishment' misreading.

statement.zh: 它没有立刻让基督教成为多数，也没有消除宗教冲突；但它改变了帝国与宗教团体之间的关系，为后来的国教化铺路。
statement.en: It did not immediately make Christianity the majority or end religious conflict, but it changed the relationship between the empire and religious communities and prepared the way for later establishment.

zh: 它没有立刻让基督教成为多数，也没有消除宗教冲突；但它改变了帝国与宗教团体之间的关系，为后来的国教化铺路。
en: It did not immediately make Christianity the majority or end religious conflict, but it changed the relationship between the empire and religious communities and prepared the way for later establishment.

note.zh: 作者判断：把“长期影响”与“ immediate 结果”分开。
note.en: Author judgment: separates long-term influence from immediate results.

statement.zh: 爱国将领祖逖不因西晋倾覆而气馁，率领亲族部曲数百人从京口渡江北上。他在江中击楫发誓：“不能清中原而复济者，有如大江！”祖逖在豫州、兖州一带联合坞堡主，屡败石勒军队，收复黄河以南大片土地。
statement.en:
The patriotic general Zu Ti, undeterred by the collapse of the Western Jin, leads a few hundred of his clansmen and troops north from Jingkou. Midway across the Yangtze, he strikes an oar and vows: 'If I cannot cleanse the Central Plains and return, may I be like this river!' In Yuzhou and Yanzhou, Zu Ti allies with local fortress lords, repeatedly defeating Shi Le's forces and recovering vast lands south of the Yellow River.

title.en: Former Roman Emperor Maximian commits suicide in Gaul

summary.en: The abdicated former emperor Maximian, opposing Constantine's rule, flees to Marseille and attempts to proclaim himself emperor but is besieged by Constantine's forces. title.en: Church council in Asia Minor discusses the Arian controversy

summary.en: As the theological dispute between the Alexandrian presbyter Arius and Bishop Alexander intensifies, a local church council is convened in Asia Minor to attempt to reconcile differences over the divinity of Christ. title.en: Tuoba Yilu, chieftain of the Tuoba Xianbei, establishes the Dai state

summary.en: The Tuoba Xianbei chieftain Tuoba Yilu, for his services in assisting the Western Jin against Han-Zhao, is enfeoffed by Emperor Min of Jin as King of Dai, formally establishing the Dai state with its capital at Shengle (present-day Horinger, Inner Mongolia). This is the embryonic state of the Tuoba tribe, laying the foundation for the later Northern Wei unification of the north

title.en: Shi Le attacks and destroys Cao Yi in Qingzhou, unifying the lower Yellow River

title.en: Large-scale southward migration of northern gentry: the 'Robes and Hats Southward Migration'

summary.en: After the fall of the Western Jin, Central Plains gentry and commoners, fleeing the wars, cross the Yangtze in great numbers with their entire clans. Prestigious families such as the Langye Wang, Chenjun Xie, and Qiaoguo Huan, accompanied by their dependents and retainers, flock to Sima Rui in Jiankang. statement.zh: 西晋灭亡后，中原士族和百姓为躲避战乱，纷纷举族南渡长江。琅琊王氏、陈郡谢氏、谯国桓氏等豪门大族携带家眷和部曲，投奔建康的司马睿。南渡人口多达百万，史称“衣冠南渡”，促进了江南的经济文化开发。
statement.en:
After the fall of the Western Jin, Central Plains gentry and commoners, fleeing the wars, cross the Yangtze in great numbers with their entire clans. Prestigious families such as the Langye Wang, Chenjun Xie, and Qiaoguo Huan, accompanied by their dependents and retainers, flock to Sima Rui in Jiankang. The number of migrants reaches over 1,000,000. This event, known as the 'Robes and Hats Southward Migration,' promotes the economic and cultural development of Jiangnan.

For Asia in 316 CE, “Large-scale southward migration of northern gentry: the 'Robes and Hats Southward Migration'” is a traceable node of Society change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Fall of the Western Jin: Han-Zhao's Liu Yao captures Chang'an; Emperor Min surrenders

summary.en: Han-Zhao general Liu Yao besieges Chang'an; food runs out and cannibalism occurs. Emperor Min of Jin is forced to surrender, and the Western Jin officially ends. Liu Yao takes Emperor Min and his officials to Pingyang. Emperor Min is humiliated and later killed by Liu Cong. The Sima family no longer has a foothold in the north.

title.en: Professorships of law are established in Constantinople

summary.en: Emperor Constantine, valuing legal education, orders the establishment of official professorships of law in the newly built capital, Constantinople, to teach Roman law. title.en: Tiwanaku culture emerges in the Andean highlands of South America

summary.en: On the high plateau south of Lake Titicaca, the Tiwanaku civilization enters a phase of expansion. Its unique stone architecture (such as the Gate of the Sun) and agricultural techniques (raised fields) profoundly influence the later Inca civilization. This culture becomes an important center of civilization in the Andes region.

title.en: Gupta Empire rises

title.en: Constantine founds New Rome on the site of Byzantium

summary.en: On September 18, 324, Constantine defeated Licinius at Chrysopolis; within three weeks the foundation rites of New Rome were held, and the city was officially inaugurated on May 11, 330. The move shifted the empire's power centre eastward.

statement.zh: 324年9月18日，君士坦丁在博斯普鲁斯海峡对岸的克吕索波利斯击败李锡尼，成为罗马帝国东西部唯一的皇帝。
statement.en: On September 18, 324, Constantine defeated Licinius at Chrysopolis on the Asian shore of the Bosporus and became sole emperor of the Roman Empire, east and west.

sources.locator: Section: Cultural life — Byzantium and Constantinople, paragraph 1
sources.excerpt: Overcoming the army of the rival emperor, Licinius, at nearby Chrysopolis, on September 18, 324, Constantine became head of the whole Roman Empire, east and west.

zh: 324年9月18日，君士坦丁在博斯普鲁斯海峡对岸的克吕索波利斯击败李锡尼，成为罗马帝国东西部唯一的皇帝。
en: On September 18, 324, Constantine defeated Licinius at Chrysopolis on the Asian shore of the Bosporus and became sole emperor of the Roman Empire, east and west.

note.zh: 日期、地点、对手与结果均取自卡片选段。
note.en: Date, place, rival and outcome are all in the card excerpt.

statement.zh: 三周内，新罗马的奠基仪式举行；330年5月11日，扩建后的城市正式启用。
statement.en: Within three weeks the foundation rites of New Rome were held; on May 11, 330, the enlarged city was officially inaugurated.

sources.locator: Section: Cultural life — Byzantium and Constantinople, paragraph 2
sources.excerpt: Within three weeks of his victory, the foundation rites of New Rome were performed, and the much-enlarged city was officially inaugurated on May 11, 330.

zh: 三周内，新罗马的奠基仪式举行；330年5月11日，扩建后的城市正式启用。
en: Within three weeks the foundation rites of New Rome were held; on May 11, 330, the enlarged city was officially inaugurated.

note.zh: 奠基与启用日期按卡片；不写“324年建成”。
note.en: Foundation and inauguration dates follow the card; the city was not 'completed' in 324.

statement.zh: 他把首都设在古希腊城市拜占庭的旧址。
statement.en: He made the old Greek city of Byzantium his capital.

sources.locator: Section: Cultural life — Byzantium and Constantinople, paragraph 1
sources.excerpt: He decided to make Byzantium his capital.

zh: 他把首都设在古希腊城市拜占庭的旧址。
en: He made the old Greek city of Byzantium his capital.

note.zh: 只写选址，不写“亲自丈量土地”。
note.en: Only the choice of site; no unsupported detail about personal surveying.

statement.zh: 帝国权力中心由此东移。
statement.en: The empire's power centre moved eastward.

sources.locator: Section: Cultural life — Byzantium and Constantinople, paragraph 3
sources.excerpt: It displaced the power centre of the Roman Empire, moving it eastward, and achieved the first lasting unification of Greece.

zh: 帝国权力中心由此东移。
en: The empire's power centre moved eastward.

note.zh: “东移”来自卡片原文 power centre ... moving it eastward。
note.en: The eastward shift is directly supported by the card.

statement.zh: 这次选择也带来希腊世界的首次持久统一。
statement.en: The choice also brought the first lasting unification of Greece.

sources.locator: Section: Cultural life — Byzantium and Constantinople, paragraph 3
sources.excerpt: It displaced the power centre of the Roman Empire, moving it eastward, and achieved the first lasting unification of Greece.

zh: 这次选择也带来希腊世界的首次持久统一。
en: The choice also brought the first lasting unification of Greece.

note.zh: 保留卡片中的“首次持久统一”，不扩写成“统一整个地中海”。
note.en: Keeps the card's 'first lasting unification'; does not inflate it into a Mediterranean union.

statement.zh: 330年启用后，君士坦丁堡成为帝国最重要的首都之一：它既是皇帝驻地和行政中心，也是教会权力的舞台，城市以财富与建筑闻名。
statement.en: After 330, Constantinople became one of the empire's principal capitals: the emperor's residence and administrative centre, a stage for church power, and a city famed for wealth and buildings.

sources.locator: Section: Cultural life — Byzantium and Constantinople, paragraph 4
sources.excerpt: Constantinople was to become one of the great world capitals, a font of imperial and religious power, a city of vast wealth and beauty, and the chief city of the Western world.

zh: 330年启用后，君士坦丁堡成为帝国最重要的首都之一：它既是皇帝驻地和行政中心，也是教会权力的舞台，城市以财富与建筑闻名。
en: After 330, Constantinople became one of the empire's principal capitals: the emperor's residence and administrative centre, a stage for church power, and a city famed for wealth and buildings.

note.zh: “皇帝驻地、行政中心”是对 imperial power 的具体化；不写“世界第一大城市”。
note.en: 'Residence and administrative centre' unpacks imperial power; avoids 'largest city in the world'.

statement.zh: 这里控制博斯普鲁斯海峡，连接黑海与地中海；半岛与金角湾提供港湾和防御。
statement.en: The site commanded the Bosporus and linked the Black Sea with the Mediterranean; the peninsula and the Golden Horn offered harbours and defence.

zh: 这里控制博斯普鲁斯海峡，连接黑海与地中海；半岛与金角湾提供港湾和防御。
en: The site commanded the Bosporus and linked the Black Sea with the Mediterranean; the peninsula and the Golden Horn offered harbours and defence.

note.zh: 地理分析，不作为史实来源；不写具体港口设施。
note.en: Geographical analysis, not a sourced factual claim; no specific harbour works.

statement.zh: 但新都的代价同样明显。它要养活庞大的宫廷、军队与市民，要靠远距离的粮食与税收；西部的旧贵族与东部的新宫廷之间，也因此长期争权。
statement.en: But the new capital carried costs. It had to feed a large court, army and population through distant grain and taxes; the old western aristocracy and the new eastern court also competed for power.

zh: 但新都的代价同样明显。它要养活庞大的宫廷、军队与市民，要靠远距离的粮食与税收；西部的旧贵族与东部的新宫廷之间，也因此长期争权。
en: But the new capital carried costs. It had to feed a large court, army and population through distant grain and taxes; the old western aristocracy and the new eastern court also competed for power.

note.zh: 结构性分析；不写具体粮船数量或税收数字。
note.en: Structural analysis; no invented grain-ship counts or tax figures.

statement.zh: 所以，324年的决定不是一次简单的迁居，而是把帝国政治的地理重心重新校准；新罗马从此成为东部的权力容器。
statement.en: The decision of 324 was therefore not a simple move of residence but a recalibration of the empire's political geography; New Rome became the container of eastern power.

zh: 所以，324年的决定不是一次简单的迁居，而是把帝国政治的地理重心重新校准；新罗马从此成为东部的权力容器。
en: The decision of 324 was therefore not a simple move of residence but a recalibration of the empire's political geography; New Rome became the container of eastern power.

note.zh: 章末判断，不替代事实陈述。
note.en: Chapter-level judgment, not a factual substitute.

title.en: First Council of Nicaea convenes, establishing basic Christian doctrine

summary.en: Emperor Constantine convenes the first ecumenical council of Christianity at Nicaea in Asia Minor, attended by about three hundred bishops. The council strongly condemns the Arian view denying the full divinity of Christ, formulates the Nicene Creed, and establishes the orthodox doctrine of the 'consubstantiality' of the Father and the Son. It also fixes the date of Easter.

title.en: Construction begins on the great defensive walls of Constantinople

summary.en: To protect the new capital, Emperor Constantine the Great orders the construction of defensive walls from the Golden Horn to the Sea of Marmara. These walls, later reinforced many times, become one of the most formidable fortification systems of the Middle Ages, protecting Constantinople for a thousand years.

statement.en:
To protect the new capital, Emperor Constantine the Great orders the construction of defensive walls from the Golden Horn to the Sea of Marmara. These walls, later reinforced many times, become one of the most formidable fortification systems of the Middle Ages, protecting Constantinople for a thousand years.

title.en: Later Zhao's Shi Le formally proclaims himself emperor and enfeoffs his ministers

summary.en: After unifying the north, Shi Le formally ascends the imperial throne, still with the state name Zhao (Later Zhao). He posthumously honors his ancestors and enfeoffs imperial clan members and meritorious officials. Although of slave origin, Shi Le is receptive to advice and promotes sinicization policies, making Later Zhao the most powerful state in East Asia at the time.

title.en: Emperor Constantine the Great formally moves the capital to Constantinople

summary.en: Constantine the Great officially moves the Roman capital from Rome to the newly built Constantinople (formerly Byzantium). The new capital, called 'Nova Roma,' has a Senate and a complete administrative structure. This move shifts the empire's center of gravity eastward to the culturally and commercially advanced Greek-speaking regions.

title.en: Constantinople founded as Nova Roma

summary.en: Emperor Constantine founded a city on Byzantium, named Nova Roma and later Constantinople, which became the millennium-long capital of the Eastern Roman Empire and a bridge between East and West.

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝君士坦丁在拜占庭旧址建城，命名新罗马，后称君士坦丁堡，成为东罗马帝国1000年都城与东西方枢纽。城市三面环水，城墙与海墙围护，港口与大道连接内陆与海上贸易；皇帝在此设宫廷、教堂与竞技场，把帝国重心东移。此后它长期是地中海世界的政治与宗教中心。
statement.en:
The Roman Emperor Constantine built a city on the site of Byzantium and named it New Rome, later called Constantinople. It became the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire for thousands of years and a hub between the East and the West. The city was surrounded by water on three sides, protected by city walls and sea walls, and its ports and highways connected inland and maritime trade. The emperor set up palaces, churches and arenas here to move the center of the empire eastward. It has long been the political and religious center of the Mediterranean world.

It sits within the timeline's chronological coverage of Byzantine Empire and urban history.

title.en: Later Zhao's Shi Hu massively constructs palaces in Yecheng, exhausting the people

summary.en: Shi Hu conscripts hundreds of thousands of laborers to build luxurious palaces, gardens, and terraces in Yecheng. He also builds a hunting park west of Yecheng, forcing people to relocate from their ancestral lands. The heavy corvée makes life unbearable for the northern people.

statement.zh: 石虎征发民夫数十万，在邺城大兴土木，修建豪华宫殿和园林台观。他还在邺城西郊建造猎场，驱赶百姓迁离故土。沉重的徭役使北方百姓苦不堪言。宫殿、台观与园苑相连，工程规模空前，民夫在严苛工期下死伤相继；猎场圈占农田，迁徙之家失去生计。奢靡与暴政消耗了后赵的国力。
statement.en: Shi Hu recruited hundreds of thousands of civilians to carry out extensive construction work in Yecheng, building luxurious palaces and gardens.

title.en: Church of the Holy Sepulchre completed

summary.en: Constantine's mother Helena builds the Holy Sepulchre at Jesus's tomb, a foremost Christian shrine.

statement.zh:
君士坦丁母后海伦娜在耶稣安葬处建圣墓教堂，成基督教圣地。

title.en: Gothic bishop Ulfilas promotes the Christianization of the Goths

summary.en: To facilitate missionary work, the Gothic bishop Ulfilas invents the Gothic alphabet and translates the Bible into Gothic. title.en: Emperor Cheng of Jin dies; Emperor Kang of Jin succeeds

summary.en: Emperor Cheng of Jin dies. As his son is too young, his brother Sima Yue ascends as Emperor Kang of Jin. Emperor Kang's reign is short, and power is dominated by the Yu clan of imperial in-laws.

statement.zh: 东晋晋成帝司马衍病逝，因其子年幼，由其弟司马岳即位，是为晋康帝。康帝在位短暂，朝政大权由庾氏外戚把持。庾亮以中书令与征讨都督的身份主持朝局，外镇与中央相互牵制；皇位在幼主与宗室之间转移，显示东晋皇权依赖门阀与方镇的支持。这样的结构使政局难以稳定。
statement.en: Emperor Cheng of Jin dies.

title.en: The Nicene Creed is reaffirmed as authoritative in the Eastern Empire

summary.en: Under pressure from orthodox factions, Constantius II convokes a church council to reaffirm the authority of the Nicene Creed and exile Arian bishops. However, because the emperor himself leans toward Arianism, the religious strife does not subside.

statement.zh: 君士坦提乌斯二世迫于正统派压力，召集教会会议确认尼西亚信经的正统地位，流放阿里乌斯派主教。但由于皇帝本人倾向阿里乌斯派，宗教纷争并未平息。会议以条文与信条划清界限，主教们在皇权的压力下反复摇摆；东西部教会的神学分歧与政治博弈交织，正统与异端的界线仍由政府裁定。
statement.en: Constantius II, under pressure from the orthodox faction, convened a church council to confirm the orthodox status of the Nicene Creed and exiled the Arian bishops.

title.en: Yu Yi of the Eastern Jin actively prepares for a northern expedition

summary.en: The Eastern Jin General Who Pacifies the West, Yu Yi, aiming to fulfill his brother Yu Liang's ambition, reorganizes the military in Jingzhou and trains troops. He sends envoys to contact Former Yan and Former Liang, attempting to coordinate a northern expedition against Later Zhao. However, due to resistance at court, the expedition never takes place.

statement.zh: 东晋安西将军庾翼为继承其兄庾亮遗志，在荆州整顿军备，训练军队，并派遣使者联络前燕和前凉，试图联合北伐后赵。但因朝廷内部阻力，北伐最终未能实施。
statement.en:
The Eastern Jin General Who Pacifies the West, Yu Yi, aiming to fulfill his brother Yu Liang's ambition, reorganizes the military in Jingzhou and trains troops. He sends envoys to contact Former Yan and Former Liang, attempting to coordinate a northern expedition against Later Zhao. However, due to resistance at court, the expedition never takes place.

For Asia in 343 CE, “Yu Yi of the Eastern Jin actively prepares for a northern expedition” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Kang of Jin dies; his young son Emperor Mu of Jin succeeds

summary.en: Emperor Kang of Jin dies, and his two-year-old crown prince Sima Dan ascends as Emperor Mu of Jin. His mother, Empress Dowager Chu, serves as regent, assisted by the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu. The Eastern Jin court becomes even more chaotic, with powerful officials vying for power.

title.en: Long-term confrontation between the Eastern Jin and northern regimes along the Huai River line

summary.en: Later Zhao is powerful, and the Eastern Jin uses the Huai River as its border. The two sides battle for years. The Eastern Jin establishes Qiao commanderies north of the Yangtze to settle southern refugees, organizes agricultural colonies, and forms a long-standing pattern of north-south confrontation.

statement.zh:
后赵强大，东晋以淮河为界，双方连年征战。东晋在江北设立侨郡，安置南渡流民，组织屯田，形成长期的南北对峙格局。侨郡以原籍名号安置移民，屯田把流民转为兵源与税源；防线依托淮河与长江之间的水网。南北对峙因此长期化、制度化。

把「东晋与北方政权长期对峙于淮河一线」放回公元344年的东晋，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: Later Zhao is powerful, and the Eastern Jin uses the Huai River as its border.

Wang Xizhi, the Eastern Jin's Sage of Calligraphy, serves as Grand Administrator of Kuaiji, socializing with famous scholars at Lanting and elsewhere. His calligraphy integrates ancient and modern styles, creating a new natural and free-spirited style. His representative work from this period, the 'Preface to the Lanting Collection,' is hailed as the 'best running script under heaven,' marking an era of self-consciousness in Chinese calligraphy.

title.en: Murong Huang of Former Yan dies; Murong Jun succeeds

summary.en: The Wenming Emperor of Former Yan, Murong Huang, dies; his son Murong Jun succeeds. Murong Jun continues his father's ambition to expand territory, employing Han gentry, and Former Yan's power continues to grow.

statement.zh:
前燕文明帝慕容皝病逝，其子慕容儁继位。慕容儁继承父亲遗志，继续扩张疆土，重用汉族士人，前燕国力进一步增强。政权在胡汉结合中吸收制度与人才，父死子继保持政策连续；对中原的觊觎推动军事扩张。前燕由此在北方角逐中占据主动。

把「前燕慕容皝去世，慕容儁继位」放回公元348年的前燕，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: The Roman Empire recruits large numbers of Germanic mercenaries to strengthen border defenses

summary.en: Due to the heavy losses in the war with Persia, Eastern Roman Emperor Constantius II vigorously recruits Germanic barbarians (Franks, Alemanni, etc.) into the army, even appointing barbarian generals to high office. This temporarily solves manpower problems but sows the seeds for future barbarian control of the Roman army.

title.en: Later Zhao tyrant Shi Hu dies; succession struggle and internal chaos erupt

title.en: Ran Min emerges during the Later Zhao civil war, gaining military control

title.en: Ran Min issues the 'Kill the Barbarians' order and proclaims himself emperor, establishing the Ran Wei regime

title.en: Aksum conquers Meroë

summary.en: Around 350 Aksum crossed the Red Sea northward and conquered a declining Meroe, ending the Kushite kingdom and shifting Nubia's centre of power into a newly Christianised order.

statement.zh:
约350年阿克苏姆跨越红海北上，征服衰落的麦罗埃，库什王国终结，努比亚的政治中心转入基督教化后的新秩序。远征把红海贸易与内陆尼罗河通道连成一体，阿克苏姆借港口与商路扩张；麦罗埃的衰亡使区域权力重组。宗教与贸易随征服扩散。

把「阿克苏姆灭麦罗埃」放回公元350年的非洲之角，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: In about 350, Aksum crossed the Red Sea and headed north to conquer the declining Meroe.

title.en: Sasanian Persia besieges and captures the Roman fortress of Amida

title.en: Former Yan's Murong Jun dies; the young Murong Wei succeeds, with Murong Ke as regent

summary.en: Former Yan Emperor Murong Jun dies. His ten-year-old crown prince Murong Wei ascends, with Murong Ke and Murong Ping serving as regents. Murong Ke is lenient and stable, preserving Former Yan's power and maintaining its strength.

Former Yan Emperor Murong Jun dies. His ten-year-old crown prince Murong Wei ascends, with Murong Ke and Murong Ping serving as regents. Murong Ke is lenient and stable, preserving Former Yan's power and maintaining its strength.

title.en: Emperor Mu of Jin dies; Emperor Ai of Jin ascends

summary.en: Emperor Mu of Jin dies without issue. The eldest son of Emperor Cheng, Sima Pi, ascends as Emperor Ai of Jin. Emperor Ai is fond of Huang-Lao (Daoist) practices, consumes elixirs, and neglects state affairs; power falls into the hands of Huan Wen.

statement.zh:
晋穆帝司马聃病逝，无子。晋成帝长子司马丕即位，是为晋哀帝。哀帝好黄老之术，服用丹药，不理朝政，大权落入桓温之手。皇位在宗室之间转移，辅政与方镇的力量随之消长；桓温借北伐与朝政扩张权势。东晋的政局更加倚重强臣。

把「东晋晋穆帝去世，晋哀帝司马丕继位」放回公元360年的东晋，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: Emperor Mu of Jin, Sima Dan, died without issue.

title.en: Eastern Jin and Former Yan confront each other along the Huai River line

summary.en: The Eastern Jin and Former Yan are separated by the Huai River, with small-scale skirmishes continuing along the border. The Eastern Jin strengthens defenses along the Huai, building fortresses, but is unable to launch large-scale northern expeditions.

statement.zh:
东晋和北方前燕以淮河为界，双方在边境地区持续发生小规模冲突。东晋加强沿淮防御，修建城堡，但无力大举北伐。淮河成为南北政权对峙的自然界线，城堡与屯戍构成纵深防御；前燕以骑兵袭扰，东晋则以水军与城守应对。双方都难以突破，边境陷入长期拉锯。

把「东晋与北方前燕对峙于淮北一线」放回公元361年的东晋，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Roman Emperor Julian launches a pagan revival movement, suppressing Christianity

summary.en: Emperor Julian (known as the 'Apostate') attempts to restore Roman traditional polytheism and vigorously suppresses Christianity. He orders the reconstruction of pagan temples, restores sacrifices, forbids Christians from teaching classical literature, and encourages sectarian infighting. However, his reign is short, and he is ultimately unsuccessful.

title.en: Emperor Ai of Jin dies; Emperor Fei of Jin ascends

summary.en: Emperor Ai of Jin dies from elixir poisoning. As he has no son, his younger brother, the Prince of Langye Sima Yi, ascends as Emperor Fei of Jin. Huan Wen continues to control the court, and the deposed emperor is a mere puppet.

statement.zh:
晋哀帝因服食丹药中毒去世，因其无子，其弟琅琊王司马奕即位，是为晋废帝。桓温继续操控朝政，废帝形同傀儡。丹药之害在东晋宫廷屡见，皇帝的健康与寿命受其影响；继位者缺乏自己的班底，军政大权集中于权臣。

title.en: Roman Emperor Julian campaigns against Persia and is killed in battle

summary.en: Emperor Julian launches an expedition against the Sasanian Persian Empire, initially making good progress. However, in a battle near Ctesiphon, Julian is overconfident and advances rashly, is wounded by a Persian spear, and dies. On his deathbed, he is said to have acknowledged, 'Galilean (Christian), you have won.'

statement.zh: 尤里安皇帝发动对波斯萨珊帝国的远征，初期进展顺利。但在泰西封附近的战役中，尤里安轻敌冒进，被波斯军击伤，不治身亡。临终前他有说法认为承认“加利利人（基督徒）胜利了”。
statement.en:
Emperor Julian launches an expedition against the Sasanian Persian Empire, initially making good progress. However, in a battle near Ctesiphon, Julian is overconfident and advances rashly, is wounded by a Persian spear, and dies. On his deathbed, he is said to have acknowledged, 'Galilean (Christian), you have won.'

For Europe in 364 CE, “Roman Emperor Julian campaigns against Persia and is killed in battle” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Crete earthquake and tsunami

summary.en: In 365 a great earthquake and tsunami strike the eastern Mediterranean, wrecking Crete, Rhodes and Alexandria in Egypt; coastal settlements are destroyed and many die, among the worst natural disasters of late antiquity.

statement.zh: 365年，东地中海发生大地震并引发海啸，克里特、罗得岛与埃及亚历山大港等地受灾，沿海聚落被毁、生灵涂炭，是古代晚期最严重的自然灾害之一。地震抬升与海啸冲刷改变了海岸线，港口淤塞、城市重建艰难；灾后救济与迁徙重塑了地方社会。灾难的记忆进入文献与纪年。
statement.en: In 365, a major earthquake occurred in the Eastern Mediterranean and triggered a tsunami.

title.en: New Roman Emperor Jovian makes peace with Persia, ceding border territories

title.en: Excavation of the Mogao Caves at Dunhuang begins

summary.en: The Former Liang monk Le Zun excavates the first cave on the cliff face opposite the Sanwei Mountains southeast of Dunhuang, for meditation and worship. Thereafter, the Mogao Caves are continuously expanded over a thousand years, becoming the world's largest and longest-lasting treasure house of Buddhist art.

statement.zh:
前凉僧人乐僔在敦煌东南的三危山对面开凿了第一个洞窟，用于禅修礼拜。此后，莫高窟历经1000年不断扩建，成为世界上规模最大、延续时间最长的佛教艺术宝库。洞窟由僧俗与地方政权共同营建，壁画与塑像层累相叠；商路与寺院经济供养工匠，佛教艺术在绿洲扎根。

把「敦煌莫高窟开始开凿」放回公元366年的前凉，可以看到宗教变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en:
The Former Liang monk Le Zun cut the first cave on the cliff opposite the Sanwei Mountains southeast of Dunhuang, for meditation and worship. Thereafter the Mogao Caves were expanded for a thousand years, becoming the world's largest and longest-lasting treasury of Buddhist art. Monks, laypeople and local regimes built them together, and paintings and sculptures accumulated layer on layer; trade routes and monastic wealth supported the craftsmen, and Buddhist art took root in the oasis.

It sits within the timeline's chronological coverage of Former Liang and religion history.

The event is treated as one node in a longer sequence of change across Asia.

The record is presented as part of the wider history of Former Liang rather than as an isolated incident.

title.en: Fu Shuang and others, brothers of Former Qin's Fu Jian, launch a rebellion

summary.en: Several brothers of Former Qin Emperor Fu Jian (Fu Shuang, Fu Liu, etc.), opposing Wang Meng's reforms, rise in rebellion. Fu Jian sends Wang Meng to suppress the rebellion, which is quickly quelled, consolidating his rule.

statement.zh:
前秦皇帝苻坚的几位兄弟（苻双、苻柳等）联合反对王猛改革，起兵反叛。苻坚派王猛率军镇压，迅速平定叛乱，巩固了统治。宗室与改革派的对立由此公开化，地方豪强借机观望；王猛以分化与速战化解危机。集权改革得以继续推进。

把「前秦苻坚同母弟苻双等发动叛乱」放回公元367年的前秦，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: Several brothers of Former Qin Emperor Fu Jian, including Fu Shuang and Fu Liu, opposed Wang Meng's reforms and rose in rebellion.

title.en: The Roman Empire and Sasanian Persia vie for control of Armenia

title.en: Huan Wen deposes Emperor Fei of Jin and establishes Emperor Jianwen of Jin

summary.en: Huan Wen leads his troops into the capital, falsely accusing Emperor Fei of impotence and inability to produce an heir, and forces Empress Dowager Chu to depose him. He then installs the emperor's brother, the Prince of Kuaiji Sima Yu, as Emperor Jianwen of Jin. Huan Wen thereby fully controls the Eastern Jin court.

statement.zh: 桓温带兵入朝，诬蔑晋废帝司马奕阳痿不能生育，逼迫褚太后废帝，改立其弟会稽王司马昱为帝，是为晋简文帝。桓温彻底掌控东晋朝政。
statement.en:
Huan Wen leads his troops into the capital, falsely accusing Emperor Fei of impotence and inability to produce an heir, and forces Empress Dowager Chu to depose him. He then installs the emperor's brother, the Prince of Kuaiji Sima Yu, as Emperor Jianwen of Jin. Huan Wen thereby fully controls the Eastern Jin court.

For Asia in 371 CE, “Huan Wen deposes Emperor Fei of Jin and establishes Emperor Jianwen of Jin” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Buddhism enters Goguryeo: a new language for royal power

summary.en: In 372 CE, influenced by China, Buddhism was introduced into Goguryeo as ideological backing for a newly centralised bureaucracy; at about the same time, Confucian education began to be emphasised. King Sosurim (r. 371–384) issued laws and decrees aimed partly at centralising royal authority, and Goguryeo emerged as a full-fledged aristocratic state.

statement.zh: 372年，受中国影响，佛教传入高句丽，为新近中央集权的官僚制提供意识形态支撑；大约同时，儒学教育开始受到重视。
statement.en: In 372 CE, influenced by China, Buddhism was introduced into Goguryeo as ideological backing for a newly centralised bureaucracy; at about the same time, Confucian education began to be emphasised.

title.en: Eastern Roman Emperor Valens persecutes orthodox Christians

summary.en: Emperor Valens, an adherent of Arianism, begins a large-scale persecution of Nicene orthodox Christians, exiling many bishops and confiscating orthodox churches. This deepens religious divisions within the Eastern Empire.

statement.zh: 信奉阿里乌斯派的瓦伦斯皇帝开始大规模迫害尼西亚正统派基督徒，流放多位主教，查封正统派教堂。这导致了东部帝国内部的宗教分裂加剧。教会财产与主教座成为争夺对象，信众按派别分化；皇帝以教义争端服务皇权，反而削弱了东部的凝聚力。宗教政治与帝国政治彼此纠缠。
statement.en: Emperor Valens, who believed in Arianism, began a large-scale persecution of Orthodox Christians in Nicaea, exiled many bishops, and closed down Orthodox churches.

title.en: Huan Wen of the Eastern Jin dies; Huan Chong voluntarily yields power; Xie An becomes the pillar

summary.en: Huan Wen, who had attempted to usurp the throne, dies. His brother Huan Chong succeeds as Inspector of Jingzhou. title.en: The Visigoths, driven by the Huns, request to enter the Roman Empire for refuge

summary.en: The Huns migrating west defeat and displace the Ostrogoths. The Visigoths, fearing the Huns, gather on the north bank of the Danube and request permission to cross into the Roman Empire for refuge. Eastern Emperor Valens grants their request.

statement.en: The Huns from the east moved westward, defeating and driving out the Ostrogoths.

title.en: Xie Xuan of the Eastern Jin forms the 'Beifu Army', training elite troops

summary.en: The Eastern Jin Chancellor Xie An orders his nephew Xie Xuan to form a new army at Jingkou (present-day Zhenjiang), recruiting northern refugees and sons of military families. title.en: The Visigoths received into the Roman Empire revolt in Thrace

summary.en: Roman officials mistreat the Visigothic refugees, even selling them into slavery. The Visigoths, pushed to the limit, revolt, defeat the local Roman garrison, and begin to plunder and ravage Thrace.

statement.zh: 罗马官员欺压进入帝国的西哥特难民，甚至将他们卖为奴隶，忍无可忍的西哥特人发动暴动，击败当地的罗马驻军，开始在色雷斯地区烧杀抢掠。
statement.en:
Roman officials mistreat the Visigothic refugees, even selling them into slavery. The Visigoths, pushed to the limit, revolt, defeat the local Roman garrison, and begin to plunder and ravage Thrace.

title.en: Fu Jian of Former Qin actively prepares to attack the Eastern Jin

summary.en: Ignoring the objections of his ministers, Fu Jian begins large-scale conscription and stockpiling of grain, preparing to attack the Eastern Jin. He forcibly conscripts all males over fifteen into the army, with a total force purportedly numbering one million.

statement.zh:
前秦苻坚不顾群臣反对，开始大规模征兵和囤积粮草，为进攻东晋做准备。他强征全国十五岁以上男子入伍，总兵力号称百万。征发把民力推向极限，粮运与军械的筹备遍及州县；朝中反对者被压制，决策愈发专断。南征的车轮已经启动。

把「前秦苻坚积极准备南征东晋」放回公元377年的前秦，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Former Qin captures the Eastern Jin stronghold Xiangyang, opening the gateway to the south

summary.en: Former Qin's large army besieges the Eastern Jin city of Xiangyang. The defending commander Zhu Xu is defeated and captured, and Xiangyang falls. Former Qin gains a strategic foothold in the middle Yangtze, paving the way for a large-scale southern campaign.

statement.zh:
前秦大军围攻东晋的襄阳，守将朱序战败被俘，襄阳陷落。前秦获得了长江中游的战略要地，为大规模南征铺平了道路。襄阳扼汉水与长江通道，得失关乎南北攻守；守城失利使东晋中线出现缺口。前秦由此取得前进基地，但南征仍受水网与补给限制。

把「前秦攻占东晋重镇襄阳，打开南方门户」放回公元378年的前秦，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Battle of Adrianople: Visigothic cavalry routs the Roman army; Valens is killed

summary.en: Eastern Roman Emperor Valens engages the Visigoths at Adrianople (present-day Edirne, Turkey) in a decisive battle. The traditional Roman infantry phalanx is outflanked and crushed by Visigothic heavy cavalry; about 40,000 Roman soldiers are killed, and Valens himself perishes. This battle marks the rise of cavalry as the dominant force on the battlefield, replacing infantry.

title.en: Former Qin continues its southern advance; the Eastern Jin situation becomes critical

summary.en: In the 4th year of Taiyuan (379), after capturing Xiangyang, Former Qin's military advance threatens the Yangtze and Huai River region. The Eastern Jin's defense lines are stretched, and the court panics. Under Xie An's command, Xie Xuan intensifies the training of the Beifu Army in preparation for the Battle of Fei River (383). Fu Jian's southern campaign plan is accelerating.

statement.zh: 东晋太元4年（379年），前秦攻陷襄阳后兵锋直指江淮。东晋沿江防线吃紧，朝廷上下恐慌。在谢安指挥下，谢玄加紧训练北府兵，为淝水之战（383年）作准备。前秦苻坚的南征计划正加速推进。
statement.en:
In the 4th year of Taiyuan (379), after capturing Xiangyang, Former Qin's military advance threatens the Yangtze and Huai River region. The Eastern Jin's defense lines are stretched, and the court panics. Under Xie An's command, Xie Xuan intensifies the training of the Beifu Army in preparation for the Battle of Fei River (383). Fu Jian's southern campaign plan is accelerating.

For Asia in 379 CE, “Former Qin continues its southern advance; the Eastern Jin situation becomes critical” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: The Athanasian Creed affirms the Trinity

summary.en: The Latin church formulated the Athanasian Creed to define the Father, Son and Holy Spirit as one Godhead, becoming a standard of orthodox belief.

statement.zh: 西方教会以《阿他那修信经》系统表述圣父、圣子、圣灵三位一体，成为正统信仰基准。信经逐条申明三个位格同质同尊，又强调道成肉身与救赎的教义结构；它并非用于礼仪诵读，而更像一份供教学与审定之用的信仰纲要。三位一体的表述在多次会议与论争中逐步定型，这份文本把此前的讨论压缩成可背诵、可考核的形式。

title.en: Theodosius issues the Edict of Thessalonica, making Christianity the state religion of the Roman Empire

title.en: The Beifu Army shows its prowess, repeatedly defeating Former Qin reconnaissance forces along the border

summary.en: The Beifu Army led by Xie Xuan launches harassing operations along the Huai River, repeatedly defeating Former Qin scouting and advance units. The formidable fighting power of the Beifu Army astonishes the Former Qin court.

statement.zh:
谢玄率领的北府兵在淮河沿线展开袭扰战，多次击败前秦的侦察和前哨部队。北府军的强悍战斗力震惊前秦朝野。北府兵以招募的北方流民为骨干，训练严格、军纪严整，熟悉淮河地形；小规模交锋的胜利积累了信心，也为后来的大战做准备。

title.en: Hinduism experiences a revival under the patronage of the Gupta Empire

summary.en: The Gupta Empire, favoring Hinduism, actively sponsors temple construction and Brahminic rituals. The scriptures of Vaishnavism and Shaivism (such as the Puranas) are codified during this period, and Hinduism overtakes Buddhism as the dominant religion in central and northern India.

statement.zh: 笈多帝国崇尚印度教，积极赞助神庙建设和婆罗门祭祀。毗湿奴教和湿婆教的经典（如《往世书》）在此期间定型，印度教在印度中部和北部压倒佛教，成为主流宗教。王室的赐地供养寺院与祭司，神庙的造像融合地方信仰；宗教的整合借助帝国的统一与贸易网络而扩展。
statement.en: The Gupta Empire advocated Hinduism and actively sponsored temple construction and Brahmin sacrifices.

title.en: The First Council of Constantinople convenes, reaffirming the Nicene Creed

summary.en: Theodosius I convenes the Second Ecumenical Council in Constantinople, which formally reaffirms the authority of the Nicene Creed and condemns Arianism, Macedonianism, and other heresies. The council also elevates the see of Constantinople to a position second only to Rome.

title.en: Xie An, unflappable, calmly deploys the Eastern Jin defense line

summary.en: Faced with the overwhelming Former Qin army, Xie An remains calm in the midst of chaos. He appoints Xie Shi as Grand Marshal of the Expedition, Xie Xuan as Vanguard Commander, leading 80,000 Beifu troops to meet the enemy. He himself remains behind, playing chess with a guest, to stabilize public morale.

statement.zh: 面对前秦大军压境，东晋宰相谢安临危不乱。他任命谢石为征讨大都督，谢玄为前锋都督，率八万北府兵迎敌，自己却在后方与人下围棋，稳定人心。
statement.en:
Faced with the overwhelming Former Qin army, Xie An remains calm in the midst of chaos. He appoints Xie Shi as Grand Marshal of the Expedition, Xie Xuan as Vanguard Commander, leading 80,000 Beifu troops to meet the enemy. He himself remains behind, playing chess with a guest, to stabilize public morale.

title.en: Xie An remains composed upon receiving the victory report, though inwardly overjoyed

summary.en: When the victory report of the Battle of Fei River reaches Jiankang, Xie An is playing chess with a guest. He glances at the dispatch and continues playing. When asked, he calmly replies, 'The children have defeated the enemy.' After the guest leaves, he is so excited that the teeth of his clogs break.

statement.zh: 淝水之战捷报传到建康，谢安正在与客人下棋。他看罢战报，若无其事地继续下棋。客人问及，他才平静地说“小儿辈大破贼”。送客后，他兴奋得连木屐的齿都折断了。
statement.en:
When the victory report of the Battle of Fei River reaches Jiankang, Xie An is playing chess with a guest. He glances at the dispatch and continues playing. When asked, he calmly replies, 'The children have defeated the enemy.' After the guest leaves, he is so excited that the teeth of his clogs break.

title.en: Murong Chui rebels against Former Qin and establishes the Later Yan regime

summary.en: Taking advantage of the chaos after the Battle of Fei River and the collapse of the north, Murong Chui, a general of Former Qin, proclaims himself King of Yan at Xingyang, establishing the Later Yan regime. He quickly rallies his old Xianbei followers, captures Yecheng, and restores the Yan state.

statement.zh: 前秦大将慕容垂乘淝水战败、北方大乱之机，在荥阳自称燕王，建立后燕政权。他迅速召集鲜卑旧部，攻占邺城，恢复燕国。慕容垂久历战阵，善于安抚降众与旧族，以复国为号召聚拢人心；后燕据河北立足，与后秦、西燕等势力争夺中原。北方再次进入多国并立的格局。

title.en: Maijishan Grottoes carved

summary.en: From Later Qin to Northern Wei, cliff caves are carved at Maijishan near Tianshui, famed for lifelike clay sculpture, 'a gallery of Eastern sculpture'.

statement.zh:
后秦至北魏在甘肃天水麦积山开凿石窟，泥塑造像灵动秀美，现存窟龛逾两百，被誉为东方雕塑陈列馆。窟龛凿于崖壁，以栈道相连，造像多为泥塑加彩，面相与衣纹随时代而变化，从秀骨清像到丰腴圆润。供养人与题记记录了地方信众的参与。

把「麦积山石窟开凿」放回公元384年的陇右，可以看到艺术变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: From the late Qin Dynasty to the Northern Wei Dynasty, grottoes were excavated in Maiji Mountain, Tianshui, Gansu Province.

title.en: Theodosius I further strengthens the position of Orthodox Christianity

summary.en: Eastern Roman Emperor Theodosius I issues a series of decrees, closing pagan temples and banning pagan activities such as the Olympic Games. Christianity becomes the sole legal religion of the empire, profoundly influencing medieval European civilization.

statement.zh: 东罗马皇帝狄奥多西一世颁布多道法令，关闭异教神庙，禁止奥林匹克竞技等异教活动，基督教成为帝国唯一合法信仰，对欧洲中世纪文明影响深远。法令把正统教义定为国教，压缩多神教的公共空间；神庙、节庆与竞技的废止改变了城市生活。宗教统一强化了皇权，也埋下后续的教义纷争。

title.en: Murong Chui of Later Yan consolidates the north, annexing most of Hebei

summary.en: Later Yan Emperor Murong Chui leads his army to capture Huatai and Luoyang, heavily defeating the Eastern Jin defenders, and gains complete control of the area north of the Yellow River. Later Yan becomes one of the most powerful states in the north.

statement.zh:
后燕皇帝慕容垂率军攻占滑台、洛阳等地，大败东晋守军，全面控制了黄河以北地区，后燕成为北方最强大的国家之一。军事胜利依托骑兵机动与对地方豪族的笼络；占据要冲使后燕获得兵源与粮道。北方诸政权在此消长中重新划分势力。

把「后燕慕容垂巩固北方，吞并河北大部」放回公元387年的后燕，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Lü Guang of Later Liang formally proclaims himself king

summary.en: Lü Guang proclaims himself King of Sanhe at Guzang, establishing an independent kingdom. He is a devout Buddhist, inviting the Western Regions monk Kumarajiva to translate scriptures in Liangzhou, which becomes a major Buddhist center.

statement.zh:
吕光在姑臧自称三河王，建立独立王国。他信奉佛教，迎请西域高僧鸠摩罗什在凉州译经，凉州成为当时的佛教中心之一。河西的军镇与商路支撑割据，译场把梵文与汉文之间的转换制度化；政权的宗教赞助提升了地方声望。凉州学风因而兴盛。

title.en: The Serapeum of Alexandria is destroyed by Christians

summary.en: With the support of Theodosius I, Theophilus, the bishop of Alexandria, leads a Christian mob to destroy the famous Serapeum temple in the city, marking the destruction of the last academic center of paganism.

statement.zh:
在狄奥多西一世支持下，亚历山大港主教提阿非罗率领基督徒暴徒，摧毁了城中著名的塞拉皮斯神庙，标志着异教最后的学术中心被毁灭。神庙兼有图书馆与学术功能，破坏使古典学术在城中失去依托；宗教冲突与帝国政策相互推动。地中海世界的知识网络因此受损。

把「亚历山大城塞拉皮斯神庙被基督徒摧毁」放回公元389年的拜占庭帝国，可以看到宗教变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Northern Wei defeats the remnants of the Tiefu Xiongnu, completely controlling the Hetao region

summary.en: Tuoba Gui of Northern Wei again campaigns west, completely eliminating the remnants of the Tiefu Xiongnu and occupying the Hetao region. Northern Wei's territory expands to the middle and upper Yellow River, surpassing Later Yan in power.

statement.zh:
北魏拓跋珪再次西征，彻底消灭铁弗匈奴的残余势力，占据河套地区。北魏的版图扩展到黄河中上游，实力超过后燕。西征把部落征服与边防经营结合，河套的农牧资源增强国力；对后燕的力量对比由此改变。草原与中原的交界成为争夺焦点。

title.en: Theodosius I holds the last ancient Olympic Games

summary.en: Theodosius I orders the holding of the last ancient Olympic Games at Olympia. He then issues an edict banning the Olympics as a pagan activity, ending a thousand-year tradition.

statement.zh: 狄奥多西一世下令，在奥林匹亚举行了历史上最后一届古代奥运会。随后他颁布法令，认为奥运会是异教活动，予以禁止，延续1000年的古代奥运会就此终结。竞技与祭祀相连，赛会既是体育盛会也是城邦敬神的场合；基督教化的帝国以禁令清除异教仪式，神庙与竞技场渐趋荒废。
statement.en:
Theodosius I ordered that the last ancient Olympic Games in history be held in Olympia. Then he issued a decree that the Olympic Games were a pagan activity and were banned. This ended the ancient Olympic Games that had lasted for thousands of years. Competitions are connected with sacrifices, and competitions are both sports events and an occasion for city-states to worship gods; Christian empires eliminated pagan rituals with bans, and temples and arenas gradually became abandoned.

It sits within the timeline's chronological coverage of Byzantine Empire and culture history.

The event is treated as one node in a longer sequence of change across Europe.

title.en: Yao Xing of Later Qin captures Luoyang from the Eastern Jin

summary.en: Taking advantage of the Eastern Jin's internal strife, Yao Xing of Later Qin sends troops to capture Luoyang, taking the Eastern Jin defenders captive. Luoyang again falls into the hands of a northern regime, and the Eastern Jin's northern gains are lost once more.

title.en: Later Yan suffers a devastating defeat at the Battle of Canhe Slope by Northern Wei, losing its elite forces

summary.en: Murong Bao, crown prince of Later Yan, leads 80,000 elite troops to attack Northern Wei. Tuoba Gui lures the enemy deep and sets an ambush at Canhe Slope (present-day Liangcheng, Inner Mongolia). The Later Yan army is routed, and tens of thousands are captured and massacred. Later Yan never recovers.

statement.zh: 后燕太子慕容宝率八万精锐进攻北魏，拓跋珪诱敌深入，在参合陂（今内蒙古凉城）设伏。后燕军大败，数万人被俘后遭屠杀。后燕从此一蹶不振。
statement.en:
Murong Bao, crown prince of Later Yan, leads 80,000 elite troops to attack Northern Wei. Tuoba Gui lures the enemy deep and sets an ambush at Canhe Slope (present-day Liangcheng, Inner Mongolia). The Later Yan army is routed, and 10,000 are captured and massacred. Later Yan never recovers.

For Asia in 395 CE, “Later Yan suffers a devastating defeat at the Battle of Canhe Slope by Northern Wei, losing its elite forces” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: The Roman Empire permanently splits into Eastern and Western halves

summary.en: Roman Emperor Theodosius I dies in Milan, dividing the empire between his two sons: Arcadius receives the Eastern Roman Empire (capital Constantinople), and Honorius receives the Western Roman Empire (capital Ravenna). Thereafter, the two halves are never reunited; the Western Roman Empire falls in 476 CE, while the Eastern Roman Empire continues until 1453 CE.

title.en: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin is killed by his concubine Lady Zhang; Sima Daozi and his brother usurp power

summary.en: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, joking while drunk that he would depose Lady Zhang, is killed by her in collusion with eunuchs while he sleeps. The death is reported as a nightmare. After his death, his younger brother Sima Daozi and Sima Yuanxian monopolize power, and the Eastern Jin court becomes even more chaotic.

title.en: Duan Ye establishes the Northern Liang regime

summary.en: Duan Ye, Grand Administrator of Jiankang of Later Liang, is supported by Juqu Mengxun and others to become Governor of Liangzhou, breaking away from Later Liang to establish an independent state, known as Northern Liang. Northern Liang is later usurped by Juqu Mengxun and becomes one of the Sixteen Kingdoms.

statement.zh:
后凉建康太守段业被沮渠蒙逊等人拥立为凉州牧，脱离后凉独立，史称北凉。北凉后来被沮渠蒙逊篡夺，成为十六国之一。河西的绿洲农业与商路是政权根基，拥立与篡夺显示军镇势力的主导；佛教与译经在凉州延续，政权更迭虽频，河西在十六国中相对安定。

title.en: Tufa Wugu establishes the Southern Liang regime

summary.en: The Hexi Xianbei chieftain Tufa Wugu proclaims himself King of Xiping at Lianchuan (present-day Ledu, Qinghai), establishing the Southern Liang regime. Southern Liang competes with Later Liang and Northern Liang for control of the Hexi Corridor.

statement.zh:

title.en: John Chrysostom, Patriarch of Constantinople, begins to lead the church

summary.en: The famous church orator John (Golden Mouth) is appointed Patriarch of Constantinople. He strongly criticizes court luxury and corruption and implements church reforms, winning the support of the people but incurring the enmity of Empress Eudoxia.

statement.zh: 著名的教会演说家约翰（金口约翰）被任命为君士坦丁堡牧首。他的讲道把批评直指宫廷奢侈腐化，并在教会内部推行改革，因此赢得民众拥护；但同样的批评也触怒了皇后欧多克西娅，使他在皇权与教会的关系中陷入对立。演说家的声望与牧首的职权在此重叠，既放大了他的影响，也放大了他的风险。

title.en: The Sun En rebellion breaks out, causing great chaos in the southeastern Eastern Jin

summary.en: Sun En of Langye, a follower of the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice, after his uncle Sun Tai is executed by the Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi, flees to an island. He gathers followers and rebels, capturing Shangyu, Kuaiji, and other places. The common people flock to him, and within ten days he commands hundreds of thousands.

title.en: Faxian departs from Chang'an for the west in search of Buddhist scriptures, heading to India

summary.en: The Eastern Jin monk Faxian, lamenting the lack of complete monastic rules in China, departs from Chang'an with companions, traversing the Hexi Corridor, the Western Regions, and crossing the Pamirs to India. After over ten years, he returns with several important Vinaya texts and writes the 'Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms'.

statement.en: The Eastern Jin monk Faxian, lamenting the incompleteness of monastic rules in China, left Chang'an with companions, crossed the Hexi Corridor and the Western Regions and passed the Pamirs to India.

title.en: The Donatist schism in North Africa becomes severe

summary.en: Within North African Christianity, a serious split arises over the issue of ordination during the Great Persecution. The Donatist faction insists that sacraments performed by traditores (those who had handed over scriptures) are invalid, forming a schism from the orthodox church. This sect has great influence in North Africa for over a hundred years.

statement.zh: 北非基督教内部因大迫害时期主教任职问题产生严重分裂，多纳图派坚持不接受背教者主持的圣事，形成与正统教会的对立。该派在西罗马帝国北非地区影响极大，持续百余年。

title.en: Easter Island begins carving giant stone statues (Moai)

summary.en: On Easter Island in the South Pacific, the Polynesian inhabitants begin carving giant stone statues (Moai) from volcanic tuff. These statues are believed to represent deified ancestors. Archaeological evidence shows that the earliest carving activity began around 400 CE.

title.en: Eastern Jin general Liu Yu distinguishes himself in the Sun En rebellion

summary.en: Liu Yu, a general of the Beifu Army, fighting against Sun En, leads from the front and repeatedly performs outstanding feats. He defeats Sun En at Juzhang, Haiyan, and other places, forcing Sun En to retreat to his island base. Liu Yu's military talent gains widespread recognition.

statement.zh: 北府兵将领刘裕在镇压孙恩起义中，身先士卒，屡建奇功。他在句章、海盐等地大破孙恩军，迫使孙恩退回海岛，刘裕的军事才能获得广泛认可。
statement.en:
Liu Yu, a general of the Beifu Army, fighting against Sun En, leads from the front and repeatedly performs outstanding feats. He defeats Sun En at Juzhang, Haiyan, and other places, forcing Sun En to retreat to his island base. Liu Yu's military talent gains widespread recognition.
